# Vivicy — exhaustive test matrix

Reconciled fingerprint: `2582e521cb1e01f71563f4523a48bdc71790082e6546de6d180cf1746862adb8` @ commit `f40acb664cf735d37f75bd5cfe1ac2f935dfbc96`


This file is the exhaustive, always-current inventory of every test case for Vivicy — every behavior the system has, whether it is covered by a test today or is a known GAP. It is **committed and machine-guarded**: the `Reconciled fingerprint` line above hashes the behavior-bearing source tree and records the HEAD commit at reconciliation time, and `scripts/test-matrix.test.ts` fails the vitest suite when code changes without this file being reconciled and re-stamped (`npm run matrix:stamp`). `git log test/TEST-MATRIX.md` is the audit trail of reconciliations. It is the single source of truth for "what should be tested" across the app (`app/`, `components/`, `lib/`) and the factory (`factory/`). It was assembled from a full per-area audit pass plus three adversarial cross-matrices (user journeys, parallel/merge chaos, process/crash chaos).

## How ids work

- Every case has a stable id: `[<area>.<n>]` for area matrices (e.g. `[extraction-gates.42]`) and `[cross.<name>.<n>]` for cross-matrices (e.g. `[cross.chaos-process.20]`). A few non-numeric suffixes (`SKILLS-GAP`, `SCOPE-NOTE`, `X4`) mark scope flags and adversarial additions.
- Ids are **stable and never renumbered**. New cases append at the next free number in their area. When a behavior is removed from the code, delete its case line — the id is retired, never reused.
- Line format: `- [id] scenario | expected outcome | kind (unit / integration / e2e-ui / e2e-process / boundary) | covered-today (test file + test name) or GAP`. A case whose line contains `GAP` anywhere is counted as a gap (including partial gaps where one half of the scenario is covered and the other is not).
- Deduplication: a full cross-file near-duplicate analysis was run at assembly time. Zero true duplicates were found — every near-identical pair (e.g. the many per-CLI "no VIVICY_TARGET_ROOT → exit 2" cases, or `retry-stage dev` via CLI vs via `POST /api/control/retry-stage`, or the factory's `computeDoneIds` vs the control plane's independent done-rule reimplementation) is a **distinct entry point or a deliberately independent reimplementation** and is kept as its own case. When a future edit makes two cases genuinely the same scenario, merge them into one line and keep **both ids** on it.

- [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.321] **Settings single-source-of-truth**: `VivicySidebar` owns `settings` state, fetched once and updated via `SettingsDialog`'s `onSaved`; `QuotaFooter` only ever reads it as a prop. - [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.322] **Triple-independent SSE subscriptions**: `ProcessControlBar`, `QuotaFooter`, and `SectionWorkflow` each open their OWN `EventSource("/api/status/stream")` rather than sharing one subscription. - [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.323] **Map-refresh triggers**: both `ProcessControlBar` (on SSE signature change) and `ProcessControlBar`'s own `act()` extract-success path call `onMapRefreshRef.current?.()`, which in `page.tsx` is wired to `loadMap(false)` (background, non-foreground) — verify a refresh triggered by EITHER path never flips a `ready` map back to a `loading`/`error` state (background loads must be non-disruptive per case app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.8). | integration | GAP
- [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.324] **Panel width CSS var vs. Sidebar's mobile Sheet width**: `page.tsx` sets `--sidebar-width` from `usePanelState().width` (24rem/36rem) for DESKTOP, but the mobile Sheet branch in `components/ui/sidebar.tsx` hardcodes its OWN `--sidebar-width: 18rem` (`SIDEBAR_WIDTH_MOBILE`) inline, overriding the page-level var scoped to that Sheet. - [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.325] **PanelToggle + panel-state cycle end-to-end**: `app/page.tsx` only renders `PanelToggle` when `state.kind === "ready"`; combined with `usePanelState`'s hydration-safe default, verify the toggle never flashes an incorrect icon/label on the FIRST paint after the map finishes loading (i.e., the "peek" server-safe default and the real persisted client state reconcile visibly, not just in isolated hook tests). | e2e-ui | GAP
- [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.326] **Accordion default-open section vs. content freshness**: `tasks` is the only section open by default; `SectionWorkflow`, `QuotaFooter`, and `ProcessControlBar` all subscribe to SSE regardless of whether their accordion section is currently collapsed/hidden — verify collapsed (but mounted, since Radix Accordion keeps content in the DOM) sections don't leak/duplicate SSE subscriptions when repeatedly expanded/collapsed (mount/unmount vs. show/hide semantics of Radix `AccordionContent` matter here). | integration | GAP

- [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.331] `NumberStepper.onChange` computes `Number(event.target.value)` on EVERY keystroke, including the transient empty string produced mid-edit by `userEvent.clear()`/backspacing all digits — `settings-dialog.test.tsx`'s clamp test only asserts the FINAL value after `user.clear(input); user.type(input, "99")`, never inspecting `setMaxParallel`/`draft.maxParallel` during the intermediate empty-string keystroke. | Traced the full chain: `Number("")` is `0` (not `NaN`), and `clampMaxParallel` in `lib/settings.ts` does `if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n < MIN_PARALLEL) return MIN_PARALLEL` — so `0` IS correctly floored to `1` (finite, and `<1`). The original flagged case (.182 and .242) correctly identifies the input/output contract as safe but nobody has written the assertion; the REAL adversarial angle is verifying no intermediate render commits a literal `0`/`NaN` to `draft.maxParallel` state that could flash into a request payload if Save fires during that exact render (e.g. a fast Enter-to-save keybinding raced with the clear). - [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.332] `hooks/use-panel-state.ts` and `hooks/use-persisted-boolean.ts` both cache a module-level `snapshot`/`store.value` that is ONLY reset via the test-only `__reset*ForTests()` escape hatches — neither hook's own file tests what happens if a consuming component mounts, the module-level snapshot gets populated, and then a SECOND unrelated test file (not resetting the store) reads a stale cross-test-file leaked value. | `beforeEach`/`afterEach` in both `.test.ts` files call the reset function faithfully, so IN THIS SUITE no leak occurs — but this is a fragile invariant enforced by test-author discipline, not by the module design (no `afterEach` is registered globally; a new test file for either hook that forgets the reset call would silently read another suite's leftover state). - [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.333] `use-persisted-boolean.ts`'s `readPersisted` treats ANY `localStorage` value other than the exact string `"true"` as `false` — this includes a value written by a DIFFERENT, incompatible schema version (e.g. if a future refactor ever persisted `"1"`/`"on"` under the same key `vivicy:quota-footer-collapsed` or `vivicy:legend-open` before rolling back). | No test constructs a "stale/foreign-format value already in localStorage from a prior app version" scenario for either `use-persisted-boolean` or `quota-footer.tsx`'s own separate `readCollapsed()` (which uses the INVERTED convention `!== "false"`, i.e. default TRUE-unless-explicitly-"false" — the opposite polarity from `use-persisted-boolean`'s default-false-unless-explicitly-"true"). This polarity mismatch between the two persistence helpers in the SAME area (one is opt-out, one is opt-in) is itself untested and undocumented as an intentional divergence — worth an explicit regression test pinning both polarities so a future "unify the two boolean-persistence helpers" refactor doesn't flip one of them by accident. | unit | GAP

- [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.335] `isEmptyPayload`'s narrowing is checked BEFORE the `!res.ok` short-circuit has a chance to matter for foreground vs background loads, but note the ORDER in `loadMap`: a background (`foreground=false`) call that receives `!res.ok` returns silently (case .8), but a background call that receives `res.ok` AND an empty-payload/ready payload STILL calls `setState` unconditionally — meaning a background refresh (via `onMapRefresh`) CAN flip a `ready` map back to `empty` if the server transiently reports `empty:true` (e.g. a race during a project switch or corpus wipe). | This directly contradicts the "background loads are non-disruptive" invariant asserted in cross-note .323/.8, which only covers the ERROR path being suppressed for background loads — it does NOT cover the EMPTY-reason path, which has no such guard in the actual code (`if (isEmptyPayload(body)) { setState(...); return }` runs unconditionally regardless of `foreground`). - [app-shell-sidebar-ui-kit.338] `hooks/use-mobile.ts`'s `subscribe` creates a NEW `matchMedia` query object (`window.matchMedia(...)`) on every subscribe call rather than reusing one across multiple simultaneous consumers (`VivicySidebar`'s `SidebarProvider`, `panel-toggle.tsx`'s indirect usage via `useSidebar`, and any other `useIsMobile()` caller) — each mounted consumer registers its OWN `matchMedia` listener rather than sharing one. | Not a correctness bug (each listener independently reflects the same live viewport), but no test verifies the listener-count/cleanup behavior when MULTIPLE components call `useIsMobile()` simultaneously and one unmounts while others remain mounted — i.e., that the shared boundary condition doesn't leak a stray `change` listener for the unmounted one while the others keep working. | unit | GAP

### Area cross-notes

- **doc-baseline <-> change-control**: `readFrozenBaselineIdentity` in change-control.ts independently re-implements "find the active frozen, non-superseded manifest" rather than calling into doc-baseline.ts — both must agree on the definition (frozen + no `superseded` marker). A drift test asserting these two independent implementations stay behaviorally identical (e.g. same manifest picked, same rejection on a superseded-only baselines dir) is a GAP: [baselines-change-requests.220] no cross-module consistency test exists between doc-baseline's freeze/supersede semantics and change-control's `readFrozenBaselineIdentity` reader.
- **doc-baseline <-> cr-apply**: cr-apply's `defaultRunFreeze` shells out to `doc-baseline.ts generate --bump patch`, which enforces `assertBumpClass` (exact patch delta) and the frozen-approval/clean-tree gates. cr-apply.test.ts always fakes `runFreeze`, so the REAL integration between cr-apply's freeze args and doc-baseline's CLI validation is never exercised end-to-end. [baselines-change-requests.221] GAP: an integration test spawning the real `doc-baseline.ts` from `cr-apply.ts`'s `defaultRunFreeze` (dirty tree, wrong bump, missing approval-by inputs) to confirm the two modules' contracts actually match at the CLI-arg boundary.
- **change-control <-> cr-apply**: `stampChangeRequestApplied` (change-control.ts) is the sole path advancing a CR to `docs_applied`, and cr-apply.ts calls it directly (not via CLI) — verified in cr-apply.test.ts's happy path (`runChangeControlCheck` passes after stamping). Good coverage here.
- **change-control <-> cr-apply (spike retirement)**: `retireAffectedSpikes` in cr-apply.ts reads `affected_verification_gates` from CR frontmatter parsed by change-control.ts's `parseFrontmatter`/`toList`. A gate value serialized as a single bare string (not `[a]`) by `serializeFmValue`/hand-authored CRs would need `toGateList`'s string-fallback branch in cr-apply.ts — this exact round-trip (create via change-control's array serialization -> read via cr-apply's list normalizer) is untested. [baselines-change-requests.222] GAP.
- **CR drafting surface <-> change-control.ts**: no leg role spawns a dedicated CR-drafting prompt — CR intake is Vivi's, inside her own turn (`factory/prompts/vivi.md`, frozen-phase section: she writes one `CR-<id>-<slug>.md` at the orchestrator-supplied id, always `status: idea` / `owner_decision: pending`, never a decision), and the apply half is the `cr-applier` leg. Vivi's inline template restates the classification enum (7 values) and the full frontmatter field set that `change-control:check` validates: [baselines-change-requests.195] GAP — no automated sync test between vivi.md's inline CR template and change-control.ts's exported `CR_CLASSIFICATIONS`/`CR_STATUSES`/frontmatter validators (the propose-never-decide half of her charter IS pinned, at [cli-supervisor-process-infra.401]).
- **cr-applier.md <-> code**: The prompt describes behavior ("touch only canonical") that only partially maps to mechanically-enforced code paths. The "touch only canonical" constraint in particular has NO code-level enforcement — only a reference-check (broken link) would incidentally catch an out-of-bounds edit that also breaks a link; an out-of-bounds edit to an unrelated file (e.g. quietly rewriting an issue's title) would sail through completely undetected. This is the single most consequential gap in the area: [baselines-change-requests.223] GAP — no allowlist/diff-scope enforcement exists to confirm the CR-applier leg's edit touched only `.vivicy/canonical/**`, unlike (for comparison) the target-repo-write allowlists likely enforced elsewhere in the factory (dev-loop legs).
- **CrReviewCards (vivi-notifications.tsx) <-> app/api/control/crs routes**: The component's contract with `/api/control/crs` and `/api/control/crs/decide` is exercised only via mocked fetch in the panel test; the actual route handlers (`app/api/control/crs/route.ts`, `app/api/control/crs/decide/route.ts`) are OUT OF THIS AREA's file list and not reviewed here, but they are the real bridge to `change-control.ts`'s `decideChangeRequest`/`readChangeRequests`. [baselines-change-requests.224] GAP (out-of-area, flagged for the API/control-plane area): no end-to-end (e2e-ui or integration) test drives CrReviewCards against the REAL API routes and a REAL change-control registry on disk — the full stack is only unit-tested in two disconnected halves.

### Adversarial additions

- [baselines-change-requests.225] `change-control.ts`'s `repoRoot` is resolved at MODULE LOAD time via `resolveTargetRoot()` (factory/target-root.ts), not lazily per-call — `VIVICY_TARGET_ROOT` changed by a test AFTER the module is first imported has no effect on the module-level `repoRoot` constant used as the default for `runChangeControlCheck({})`/`readChangeRequests(undefined)` and the CLI entry's `repoRoot` check; every existing test avoids this by always passing an explicit `{ repoRoot }`, so the env-var-driven default path (`resolveTargetRoot()` returning null when unset, vs a stale value from a prior test's env mutation in the SAME process) is completely untested and could produce cross-test leakage in a single `node:test` worker. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.226] `resolveTargetRoot(env)` with `VIVICY_TARGET_ROOT` set to whitespace-only (e.g. `"   "`) returns `null` (the `.trim().length > 0` guard) — same boundary as doc-baseline.ts's own targetOverride check, but never exercised for change-control's copy of the same logic (target-root.ts) nor for doc-baseline.ts's inline duplicate. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.227] `matchesPattern`'s generic `/**` branch (used by `.vivicy/architecture-map/viewer/**`, `docs/governance/**`, `docs/reviews/**`, `docs/spikes/**`, `_tmp/**`, `node_modules/**`, `dist/**`) has a documented-by-code but never-asserted quirk: `path.endsWith(\`/${prefix}\`)` and `path.includes(\`/${prefix}/\`)` make a pattern like `dist/**` also match a path such as `nested/dist` (no trailing content) or `a/dist/b` even though `dist/**` intends only paths physically rooted under a top-level `dist/` directory — a same-named nested directory anywhere in the tree (e.g. `.vivicy/canonical/dist/notes.md`, or `vendor/node_modules/pkg/notes.md`) is silently excluded from the corpus with no test proving or disproving this over-broad matching. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.228] `isExcludedDirectory`'s `path.endsWith(\`/${prefix}\`)` branch means a directory literally named e.g. `not_node_modules` is NOT excluded (correct, since it doesn't end with `/node_modules` as a full segment) — but a directory nested as `.vivicy/canonical/sub/node_modules` (a doc author accidentally naming a subfolder `node_modules`) IS excluded and walk() never descends into it, silently dropping any canonical `.md` files inside from the corpus with no error surfaced to `generate` or `verify` — a silent data-loss boundary with zero test coverage. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.229] `collectIncludedFiles`'s non-glob include branch (`if (!pattern.includes("*"))`) is dead code for the CURRENT `defaultInclude` (`[".vivicy/canonical/**/*.md"]`, which always contains `*`) — this code path only activates if a future include pattern is a literal path; no test exists (and arguably none can exist without editing `defaultInclude`) confirming `addIfIncluded`'s exact-match branch actually fires end-to-end via `generate`, only via the narrower `matchesPattern` unit-level reasoning in case .36. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.230] `verify`'s file-tamper detection loop only ever fires `failures.push` for `removed`/`changed`/`new included file` — a file whose PATH case changes on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS default) but whose content is identical would produce two entries in `currentByPath`/`manifestByPath` keyed by literally different strings, surfacing as a spurious simultaneous "removed: X" + "new included file: x" pair; no test exercises case-sensitivity boundary behavior on the file path key. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.231] `parseArgs` boundary: a flag repeated twice (e.g. `--version 1.0.0 --version 2.0.0`) silently lets the LAST occurrence win (object key overwritten), with no "duplicate flag" detection or error — untested silent-override behavior distinct from the missing-value case in .72. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.232] `assertBumpClass`'s `previousVersion` parameter is validated via `assertVersion` (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), but `patchBump`/`assertBumpClass`'s destructured `[M, m, p] = previousVersion.split(".").map(Number)` boundary at `p = 9007199254740991` (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) or a previous version with leading zeros (e.g. `"1.0.01"`) — the regex `\d+` allows leading zeros, so `"1.0.01"` passes assertVersion but `Number("01")` silently becomes `1`, potentially producing an expected-bump string that doesn't match the manifest's own recorded string form; untested. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.233] `readGitEvidence`'s `git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"])` failing (e.g. a freshly-initialized repo with zero commits — `HEAD` doesn't resolve) while `git status --porcelain` still succeeds produces `available: false` (since `headSha.ok` is false) even though the working tree could otherwise be clean — the "empty repo, no commits yet" boundary for a first-ever freeze attempt is untested and would always refuse freezing with a somewhat misleading "git must be available" message rather than a more specific "no commits yet" one. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.234] `supersedePriorFrozenManifests` iterates `readdirSync(baselineDirAbsolute, { withFileTypes: true })` in filesystem/OS-dependent (not sorted) order — when TWO OTHER prior frozen, non-superseded manifests exist (a data-integrity anomaly that should never happen given "at most one active frozen baseline" but isn't itself enforced anywhere), BOTH get stamped superseded in whatever order readdir yields, not a single deterministic one; no test constructs this multi-prior-frozen scenario to confirm the loop truly supersedes all of them (not just the first) as the comment intends. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.235] `stableJson`/`sortKeys` recursion has no cycle/depth guard — a manifest is always a plain JSON-round-tripped object so a circular reference can't occur in practice, but `sortKeys` is also reused nowhere else defensively; not a real GAP to test (flagging as considered, not a miss) — no case needed.
- [baselines-change-requests.236] `change-control.ts`'s `CR_FILENAME` regex (`^CR-(\d{4})-[a-z0-9-]+\.md$`) requires the slug to be lowercase/digits/hyphens only — a hand-authored CR file with an UPPERCASE letter in its slug (e.g. `CR-0001-Fix-Bug.md`) fails the filename match silently: `readChangeRequests`'s `file.match(CR_FILENAME)` returns null, so `fileNumber` becomes `null`, and the CR is then flagged via `cr_id_filename_match` (fileNumber===null branch) rather than a dedicated "malformed filename slug" message — untested distinction between "wrong number" and "unparseable slug" causes of the same error. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.237] `parseFrontmatter`'s line regex `^([a-z_]+):\s*(.*)$` only matches lowercase-plus-underscore keys — a frontmatter line with a key containing a digit or hyphen (e.g. `resulting-baseline-id:` or `field2:`) is silently DROPPED from the parsed object (the `if (!km) continue` branch), not merely mis-typed — meaning a subtly malformed CR (typo'd key name) fails open (missing field => "missing" in the checker) rather than failing loud; untested "unparseable frontmatter line is silently dropped, not reported" behavior. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.238] `renderNewChangeRequest`'s frontmatter field ordering is a HARD-CODED literal list — `rewriteFrontmatter`'s "keys not yet in the block are appended just before closing ---" branch (case .140) is only reachable in production if `decideChangeRequest`/`stampChangeRequestApplied`'s `patch` object ever contains a key absent from the writer's template; today every `patch` key (`status`, `updated_at`, `owner_decision*`, `previous_baseline_*`, `resulting_*`) IS already present in the template, so the "append new key" branch is CURRENTLY DEAD CODE in the real call graph and only reachable via a direct unit test constructing a hand-written CR missing a key — worth flagging that no test proves this actually-reachable-only-via-drift branch still works today. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.239] `readChangeRequests`'s directory-listing sort (`readdirSync(dirAbs).sort()`) is a plain lexicographic string sort — `CR-0010-x.md` sorts BEFORE `CR-0002-x.md` is false (both are zero-padded to 4 digits so lexicographic == numeric here), but a NON-zero-padded or hand-renamed file (e.g. a stray `CR-10-x.md` that fails `CR_FILENAME` anyway) would sort out of numeric order — low-value edge, but the ASSUMPTION that lexicographic sort equals numeric sort for the id scheme is never explicitly asserted by a test with CR-0001/CR-0002/.../CR-0010+ (10 or more CRs), only ever tested with 1-3 CRs. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.240] `cr-apply.ts`'s `retireAffectedSpikes` calls `flipSpikeStatus` (factory/spike-prover.ts, OUT of this area's reviewed file list but load-bearing) which THROWS if the target spike file has no `## Traceability` heading or no `status:` line inside it — `retireAffectedSpikes` does NOT catch this; an exception here would propagate up through `applyChangeRequest`'s synchronous call (not awaited, but `flipSpikeStatus` is sync and un-try/catch'd) as an UNHANDLED throw that aborts the whole `applyChangeRequest` promise with a raw error instead of a `blocked` terminal report — meaning a malformed spike file (missing Traceability block) crashes the apply chain ungracefully rather than producing an honest `phase: "retire_spikes"` block; completely untested. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.241] `defaultRunFreeze`/`defaultRunExtraction`/`defaultCommitApplied` all shell out via `spawnSync`/`spawnSync("node", ...)` with NO timeout configured — a hung child process (e.g. extract-issues.ts or doc-baseline.ts stuck waiting on stdin, or an infinite loop) blocks `applyChangeRequest` forever with no kill/timeout safety net; no test exercises a timeout/kill-on-hang scenario for any of the three real subprocess seams (all always faked in cr-apply.test.ts). | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.242] `CrReviewCards`' `decide()` has no guard against a DOUBLE-CLICK / re-entrant call while `deciding === id` is already truthy — the `AlertDialogAction onClick={onConfirm}` is not itself disabled while busy (the trigger Button disables on `deciding !== null || outcome`, but the trigger is already closed once the dialog is open), so a user could in principle trigger a second decide POST for the same CR by re-opening/re-confirming rapidly before `finally` clears `deciding`; no test asserts single-flight/idempotent-decide behavior under rapid double-confirm. | GAP
- [baselines-change-requests.243] `CrReviewCards`' i18n calls (`t("approveBlockedToastTitle", {id})`, `errorText(tErrors, \`control.${body.code}\`, fallback)`, etc.) assume every referenced translation key exists in the `crs`/`errors` message catalogs for every supported locale — no test (in this area) verifies the catalog actually DEFINES `sectionTitle`, `via`, `approve`, `reject`, `approveDialogTitle`, `approveDialogDescription`, `rejectDialogTitle`, `rejectDialogDescription`, `cancel`, `approvedToastTitle`, `rejectedToastTitle`, `approveBlockedToastTitle`, `decisionFailedToastTitle`, `networkError` for EVERY locale the app ships (a missing key in one non-English locale would render next-intl's fallback/error behavior, not a translated string) — a catalog-completeness test for this component's specific key set is a GAP. | GAP

### factory/install-skills.ts (one installed set, one settle marker)

- [cli-supervisor-process-infra.517] `report.installed` is the project's FULL installed set on every path and at every phase — auto, explicit, remove, skip, and the in-flight reports in between — computed once by `projectInstalledSet` as the ids of vivicy.json's `skills` declaration unioned with the prior report (the same union the cap and the `not_installed` refusal already call "installed") plus this run's installs, minus its removals. Two surfaces reading one file may never disagree about which skills a project has: before this, a second run or a single explicit install reset it to that run's own installs while the block and the summary count stayed whole | after a second auto run and after an explicit install, `installed` lists both runs' skills; a removal lists the survivors; the in-flight report already carries the set so no surface shows an empty project mid-run | unit, invariant (one source of truth for the installed set) | install-skills.test.ts ("a second auto run reports both baselines' skills, with only its own contribution in added" + "an explicit install reports the full set too, and every surface reads the same one" + "the in-flight report already carries the project's set, so no surface shows an empty project mid-run" + "a removal reports the shrunken set and names only what it dropped")
- [cli-supervisor-process-infra.518] The run's own contribution stays visible beside that set as `added`/`removed` (ids), and it is what the human-facing counts are built from — the green summary reads "N installed, M dropped, R rejected this run; project total T/6" (the dropped clause only when the round dropped something, and R counts VERDICTS alone, never a transport row or a failed removal the round will retry) — so the run half and the project half can never be misread as each other beside a card listing T skills | added/removed carry only this run's ids on every path; the auto round that drops one and installs one reads "1 installed, 1 dropped, 0 rejected"; `vivicy skills install --json` surfaces `added` and `removed` beside the full `installed` | unit | install-skills.test.ts ("green path: scout selection -> audits -> install -> report + vivicy.json merge + the block in both documents" + "every drop frees a slot the same round can spend, so a saturated project still evolves") + cli.test.ts ("explicit ids ride --ids and surface mode explicit")
- [cli-supervisor-process-infra.519] The skills block is a PROJECTION of `report.installed`, never a second computation of the set: the block a leg reads and the report every UI reads are one value rendered twice, in the same order, with the same metadata (priority this-run > prior report > derived from the id) and the same bundle path — in BOTH governance documents, since the two agent CLIs read different files | each document's bullets equal `report.installed` id-for-id, name-for-name, official-for-official and path-for-path after an auto run, an explicit install, a hand-declared addition and a removal | unit, invariant (the report and the block cannot state different things) | install-skills.test.ts ("a second auto run…", "an explicit install…", "a skill an owner declared by hand in vivicy.json joins the set and the block, and a skipped run converges both", "a removal reports the shrunken set…" — all four through `assertReportAgreesWithSkillsBlock`)
- [cli-supervisor-process-infra.520] An id declared in vivicy.json that no report ever described joins the set and the block with everything derivable from the id derived (`source`, `skill`, `name`, `official`) and NOTHING claimed: no audits, no security waiver. ### Area cross-notes

- **CLI/API parity seam (documented, not tested here).** `factory/cli.ts` and `lib/control.ts` deliberately do NOT share code (per the file's own CLI↔app parity header) — parity is asserted by both spawning the same factory scripts with the same args/env and reading the same state files. This area's tests only exercise the CLI side; there is no test IN THIS AREA that proves `lib/control.ts` (out of scope) actually agrees byte-for-byte with `cli.ts`'s lock schema, script names, or exit-code mapping. A parity-drift bug (e.g. someone changes `RUN_STATE_FILE` or the lock schema in one file but not the other) would not be caught by any test in this list. This is the single biggest structural gap for the area, and it is a GAP by construction since one half of the parity pair is out of scope.
- **Lock byte-compatibility is asserted only structurally.** cli.test.ts checks the on-disk lock JSON schema (`pid/target_root/mode`) and asserts the lock path equals `getProjectRuntimeDir(target)` — the very function `lib/control.ts` derives from — so the two clients can no longer disagree by construction; what is still untested is a REAL cross-process handoff (a CLI-started run probed by the app process).
- **`lib/spawner.ts` / `lib/node-spawner.ts` have NO test file at all** in this area's file list (no `spawner.test.ts` / `node-spawner.test.ts` exist), despite being critical detached-process infrastructure (real agent spawning, kill-group signal handling, fake-spawn E2E seam). Every case under those two files (30–37 above) is a GAP. This is the largest concentration of untested surface in the whole area.
- **`factory/dev-status.ts` has NO dedicated test file** despite being read-only but logic-heavy (verdict state machine, quota formatting). Its output is only exercised indirectly, and shallowly, through `cli.test.ts`'s `status` verb tests (which stub or use the real script but only assert a couple of fields: `issues_total`/`issues_done`), never its verdict state machine, quota formatting, or stale-detection directly. (`factory/dev-preflight.ts` owns `factory/dev-preflight.test.ts` since it stopped being a read-only probe: it heals the project's pinned skills at the dev-loop's start path, and the file drives that on a real git target, real cache and real notifications.)
- **`factory/target-root.ts` and `factory/sleep-sync.ts` have NO dedicated test files.** `target-root.ts`'s `resolveTargetRoot()` is exercised only as a side effect of `test-target-root.ts` always setting the env var before any test runs — the "unset" and "explicit env param" code paths are never hit by any test. `sleep-sync.ts` is invoked by `progress-ledger.ts`'s lock-retry loop but never itself timing-tested.
- **Import-order fragility is real and undocumented by a regression test.** `test-target-root.ts`'s own header comment explains that `progress-ledger.ts` (and other factory modules) bind `resolveTargetRoot()` at MODULE LOAD TIME, so the temp-root-setting import must run first. If a future refactor reorders imports in any `*.test.ts` file, or if `progress-ledger.ts` moved its `const repoRoot = resolveTargetRoot()` inside a function, this invariant would silently break (tests would target the real environment's unset root) with no test catching the regression itself — the fragility is structural, not policed by a meta-test.
- **Concurrency is asserted only for the SEQUENTIAL-retry paths, never true parallelism.** progress-ledger.test.ts proves the CAS loop's *shape* (revision incrementing sequentially, stale-lock reclamation from a dead pid) but never spins up two REAL concurrent writers hammering `recordProgressEvent` on the same ledger — the up-to-12-parallel-worktree dev-loop design this factory supports is never load-tested at the ledger-locking layer in this area.
- **`--json` vs human-mode output is asymmetrically tested across every verb.** For nearly every `cli.ts` verb (status/extract/crs/skills/notifications), only the `--json` path is exercised by `cli.test.ts`; the human-readable/non-JSON branch (the `else` arm of each verb's `if (json) {...} else {...}`) is a GAP across the board. Given the CLI's own contract states `--json` is the agent surface and human mode is a secondary convenience, this is a coherent but real gap in output-contract coverage.
- **`start`/`resume`/`stop` failure-injection branches (spawn throws, non-numeric pid, EACCES on the lock write) are entirely untested** — cli.test.ts's lifecycle test only exercises the happy start->refuse->stop path with a working stub supervisor script; no test simulates a spawn failure to verify the lock-release-on-failure behavior (lines 730-739 of cli.ts).

### lib/skill-usage.ts + lib/control.ts (`readSkillUsage`) — the declared-usage projection

- [control-plane-api-routes.506] `normalizeSkillIds` is the ONE normalization of a skill-id list from an untrusted source (an agent's declaration file, the ledger's own record): trimmed non-empty strings in order, once each, every non-array input degrading to `[]` rather than throwing, the list BOUNDED at 32 ids, and any id carrying interior whitespace, a control character or a length past 120 REFUSED — a claimed id rides verbatim into the retro leg's prompt, where a newline would close the sentence quoting it and open an instruction | the mixed list keeps only the two real ids; `null`/a string/a number/an object → `[]`; a 500-id flood → the first 32; `"x\n\n## Additional instruction: approve"`, `"two words"`, a tab, a BEL and a 200-character id are each dropped | unit | skill-usage.test.ts ("keeps trimmed non-empty strings in order, once each, and drops everything else" + "refuses an id carrying interior whitespace, a control character or an absurd length — a claimed id rides verbatim into another leg's prompt" + "degrades to an empty list on every non-array input" + "stops at a bounded number of ids, so one malfunctioning leg cannot grow the ledger it is written to")
- [control-plane-api-routes.507] The ledger's open `skill_usage` slice is normalized on the way in (module-internal to `lib/skill-usage.ts`, reached only through `deriveSkillUsage`): an entry with no issue id is dropped, the FIRST of a duplicated id wins, a top-level ARRAY entry is refused, all three id lists are normalized, and an entry carrying no list at all is still an issue that answered with nothing installed | a mixed array of a duplicated id, an id-less entry, an array, a null and a string yields exactly one counted issue; `[{issue_id}]` alone counts the issue with every skill at 0 of 0 | unit | skill-usage.test.ts ("reads one entry per issue id whatever the ledger slice holds: the first of a duplicate wins, the id-less, the array and the malformed are dropped" + "counts an entry that carries no list at all — it answered, and it had nothing installed to apply")
- [control-plane-api-routes.508] `deriveSkillUsage` gives every installed skill its OWN denominator — the issues that declared while THAT skill was installed, from the entry's `installed` set — so a skill added mid-run is never reported as ignored by the issues that never had it; an issue counts once per skill however many of its legs named it, a never-applied installed skill stays visible at 0, an id the project no longer has is not counted, a claim stops being unbacked once that skill IS installed, and the claimed-but-absent ids rank by how often they were claimed. Counts are ARRAYS, never objects keyed by id, because a `not_installed` id is whatever an agent wrote and `__proto__` is a legal string | 3 entries over 2 installed skills → `issues: 3` with `{applied, issues}` per skill; a skill installed only for the last issue reads `1 of 1` beside another's `2 of 3`; a `__proto__` claim counted twice ranks above a single one; installing a previously-claimed id empties it from `not_installed`; garbage or absent entries give zeroed counts, never a throw; an empty installed set names no skill at all | unit | skill-usage.test.ts ("counts issues per installed skill and keeps a never-applied skill visible at zero" + "gives each skill its OWN denominator — the issues that had it installed — so a skill added mid-run is never blamed for the ones before it" + "counts an issue once per skill however many times its legs declared it" + "never counts an id the project does not have, and ranks the claimed-but-absent ones by how often they were claimed" + "stops calling a claim unbacked once the project actually installs that skill" + "returns zeroed counts rather than throwing when the ledger slice is garbage or absent" + "reports no skills at all when the project has none, whatever the ledger holds")
- [control-plane-api-routes.509] `reportedSkillIds` projects the skills report's installed entries onto their ids at the boundary, tolerating every malformed shape (a non-array `installed`, a non-object entry, a non-string id, a null report) | ids only, malformed dropped, `[]` on a null/undefined report | unit | skill-usage.test.ts ("projects the installed entries onto their ids and tolerates every malformed shape")
- [control-plane-api-routes.510] `lib/control.ts#readSkillUsage(report)` is a VIEW over the progress ledger the dev loop already writes — no store of its own — and takes the report as an argument rather than re-reading it, so one response can never mix two reads; a project with NO installed skills never opens the ledger at all (three surfaces poll this route, one of them on every status frame), and a missing, empty or unparseable ledger answers with a zero denominator instead of throwing | 3 ledger entries over a 2-skill report → per-skill `{applied, issues}` and the dropped claim; absent / `{}` / `"{ not json"` → zeroed counts; a null or empty report → `applied: []` with no ledger read, even with the target root deleted | unit | control.test.ts ("counts the ledger's per-issue declarations against the project's installed set" + "answers with an empty denominator — never a throw — when the ledger is absent or unreadable" + "names no skill — and never opens the ledger — when the project has none, since three surfaces poll this route")

### Area cross-notes

- **CLI/API parity:** `lib/control.ts`'s header doc explicitly states the Next API routes and the `vivicy` CLI (`factory/cli.ts`, out of this area's file list) are two independent clients of the SAME control-plane functions and the SAME on-disk state (run-state.json, extraction-status.json, CR registry, cr-apply reports). No test in this area cross-checks that a CLI-started run (which would write run-state.json directly via `cli.ts`, not through `lib/control.ts`) is correctly picked up as `run_active:true` by `readDevStatus` invoked from the UI route — this parity claim rests entirely on both clients reading the identical file path/schema, which `lib/control.test.ts` and the route tests do not jointly verify (the CLI script itself is out of scope for this area, but the SHARED FILE CONTRACT would be a natural integration point). GAP.
- **Two independent single-run locks, two different concurrency-safety mechanisms:** the supervisor lock (`run-state.json`, atomic `wx` + pid liveness) and the skills-install lock (`skills-install.lock`, same `wx`+pid pattern) are structurally identical but exercised with very asymmetric test depth — the supervisor lock has direct tests for "holds atomically before spawn returns" and "releases on spawn throw" (control-plane-api-routes.13, .28), while the skills lock has NEITHER (control-plane-api-routes.74, .76 are GAPs). Since `startSkillsInstall` is reachable both directly and via `retry-stage` stage="skills", a lock bug there would surface identically in both call paths and neither exercises the raw lock file.
- **Both settings tiers publish through the repo's ONE atomic file writer** (`replaceFileAtomically`, shared with the managed-block engine), so an interrupted save leaves the previous document whole and a governed tree free of temps (control-plane-api-routes.341). There is still no LOCK: two concurrent writers are last-write-wins by rename, untested (control-plane-api-routes.519).
- **Route response-shape inconsistency across the area:** most `control/*` routes wrap payloads in `{ok, ...}`; `app/api/status/route.ts` does NOT (`readDevStatus` payload returned raw, and its error branch also omits `ok`). Any shared client-side response parser assuming a uniform `{ok:boolean}` envelope across `/api/status` and `/api/control/*` would break silently — this cross-route shape contract has no test anywhere verifying the two families deliberately diverge (or asserting the divergence is intentional and stable).
- **`getSpawner()` fake-vs-real switch (`VIVICY_FAKE_SPAWN=1`) is invisible to every route/lib test in this area** — all tests inject a hand-built fake `Spawner` directly into `lib/control.ts` functions, never through `getSpawner()`/`lib/spawner.ts`. The switch itself and the fake's process table are covered in cli-supervisor-process-infra (`lib/spawner.test.ts`, .304-.309/.493/.494), but the fake's script-name dispatch and file side effects (writing a fake extraction-status.json, a fake vivi-turn reply file) still have no coverage from either side. GAP.
- **Every route's notification vocabulary is declared, not invented**: `appendNotification` takes a `NotificationInput` typed against `lib/notification-events.ts`, so a typo'd `stage`/`event` fails typecheck at the call site and a key's values cannot be omitted. What each route still owns alone is the LEVEL and the framing sentence it writes into `message` beside the params — no gate holds those two in agreement with the catalogue copy.
- **`decideCr`'s `decidedBy` hardcoding is a security-relevant provenance guarantee** (the route always passes the `DECIDED_BY = "owner:ui"` constant, never trusting request input), with zero test proving a malicious/malformed body field named `decidedBy` is ignored server-side (control-plane-api-routes.165). This is exactly the kind of implicit contract that regresses silently if the route is refactored to spread the body into the `decideCr` input.
- **Total absence of route tests for three of the ten `app/api/*` route files in scope**: `crs/route.ts`, `crs/decide/route.ts`, and `transcript/[...path]/route.ts` have NO `route.test.ts` at all (confirmed via `find`), unlike every sibling route in `control/*`. `status/route.ts`, `status/stream/route.ts`, `start/route.ts`, `stop/route.ts`, `resume/route.ts`, and `agents/health/route.ts` are likewise untested at the route level (only their underlying lib functions have unit tests) — this is the single largest concentration of GAPs in the area.

### factory/agent-spawn.ts

`factory/agent-spawn.test.ts` covers four layers directly: the prompt-resolution seam (`readPrompt` / `legRoles`), the transcript taxonomy (`TRANSCRIPT_DIRS` / `issueTranscriptDir` / `transcriptDirRel`, plus the on-disk landing through a real spawn), the machine-isolation contract (the per-CLI flag sets, the env carve-out and its provider families, the credential-store-aware transcript lookups), and one end-to-end spawn through a fake `claude`/`codex` on PATH that proves the flags and the isolated env actually reach the process. Twelve rows below are still GAP, all of them in the spawn/capture half that dev-loop.test.ts's injected `steps.runImplementer/runReviewer` fakes bypass entirely: the rollout cwd filter (.252–.255) is the biggest of them — it is the load-bearing mechanism for "transcripts are attributed to the right issue under N-way concurrency" — and the rest are the spawnTee/combinedOutput passthroughs (.245, .246), the mid-walk ENOENT tolerance (.251), `ensureTranscriptDir`'s idempotence (.256), the two leg-runner compose/capture semantics (.259, .260), the `cwdFilter` passthrough (.261) and the 0-byte capture rule (.350).

### factory/leg-deps.ts

`factory/leg-deps.ts` is the ONE `LegDeps` binding every stage outside the dev loop spawns through — extraction (extractor/verifier/lens), acceptance, retro, document preparation, language detection, skill scouting, CR application, spike proving and Vivi — built from a single object literal so the rooting cannot fork per stage. It exports exactly two prompt contracts: `legDepsForTarget` (role prompt composed, then the stage's per-run context appended) and `legDepsForVerbatimPrompt` (a prompt `lib/vivi.ts` already assembled whole, role template discarded), the second of which is [upload-vivi-chat.197]. The dev loop's own `legDeps` stays in `factory/dev-loop.ts`: it injects the per-issue directives and sets a real `cwdFilter` whenever its legs run against a worktree exec root.

- [dev-loop-worktrees-merge.360] `legDepsForTarget` composes the role prompt through dev-loop's REAL `composePrompt`, so every slot that source owns (`issue_id`, `issue_path`, `graph_refs`, the vicious-defect and torture-criteria and proof-class taxonomies) is filled with no per-stage wiring and none of them can reach a leg as a literal placeholder — and it appends the stage's per-run context AFTER composing, never before and never by composing the concatenation: the role the leg must obey leads, and slot-shaped text a stage splices into its context (a CR body, prior-attempt feedback — quoted evidence, not a template) stays literal. | exact composed string; zero `{{` left from the owned slots; `{{issue_id}}` inside the context surviving unsubstituted | unit | leg-deps.test.ts ("legDepsForTarget composes the role prompt and appends the run context AFTER it" + "legDepsForTarget carries the REAL composePrompt, so a leg gets no unfilled slot and no per-stage wiring" + "the run context is appended AFTER composition, so slot-shaped text a stage splices in stays literal")
- [dev-loop-worktrees-merge.361] `legDepsForTarget` roots the leg at the TARGET repo: `abs(rel)` resolves against the given root (an already-absolute rel wins, per `node:path` resolve), `execRoot` is that root, and `cwdFilter` is null, which is what distinguishes this binding from dev-loop's own `legDeps`. | resolved paths exact; execRoot identical; cwdFilter null | unit | leg-deps.test.ts ("legDepsForTarget roots the leg at the target repo: abs() resolves against it, execRoot is it, and cwdFilter stays null")
- [dev-loop-worktrees-merge.362] The binding hands the leg dev-loop's real `agentCliArgs`, not a stage-local stub, so model/effort flags are spelled per provider from one source. | `["--model", …, "--effort", …]` for claude, `["-m", …, "-c", 'model_reasoning_effort="…"']` for codex | unit | leg-deps.test.ts ("legDepsForTarget hands the leg dev-loop's real agentCliArgs, per provider")
- [dev-loop-worktrees-merge.363] Both bindings are built from ONE object literal, so only `composePrompt` may differ between them: for the same root they agree on `abs`, `execRoot`, `cwdFilter` and `agentCliArgs`. A field added to one and not the other, or a shared field carrying a different VALUE, is the fork this pins against — the key sets are compared and then every field but `composePrompt` is compared by value (functions by their result), so neither an extra field nor a diverging one survives. | key sets deep-equal; every non-prompt field equal across both builders; `agentCliArgs` the same imported reference | unit | leg-deps.test.ts ("both bindings share ONE rooting — only the prompt differs")

A caller earns that either by spawning exactly ONE leg per run — in which case async is already fine, as `factory/detect-language.ts` demonstrates with `runCodexLegAsync` (its only caller awaits it before binding a leg of its own) — or, when it fans OUT, by the spawn being synchronous: `factory/map-review.ts` fires every lens under a single `Promise.all` and they serialize only because `runLegForProvider` (`factory/extract-issues.ts`) calls the sync `runClaudeLeg`/`runCodexLeg`. Moving a MULTI-LEG caller to the `*Async` variants therefore owes that caller a real `cwdFilter` first. | a caller switching to the async runners under a fan-out is refused, or carries a cwdFilter | unit | GAP — nothing red-flags the switch; the invariant lives only in AGENTS.md and this row

### Area cross-notes

- **Prompt-content tests exist only for implementer.md + reviewer.md** (dev-loop.test.ts:2091, 2109, 2144); merge-resolver.md and readiness-checker.md have ZERO content-assertion tests despite both encoding load-bearing contracts (the verdict-file JSON shapes the orchestrator parses via `readMergeResolutionVerdict` / `readReadinessVerdict`, and the traceability-preservation rule `issueUpdatePreservesTraceability` enforces). A prompt edit that silently breaks the documented verdict shape would only be caught by the e2e-process tests happening to exercise that exact JSON shape via their fakes — the fakes hardcode the shape independent of the prompt text, so a prompt/orchestrator-contract drift is currently invisible to the suite.
- **agent-spawn.ts's spawn/capture half still carries twelve GAP rows, the cwd-filter family the heaviest.** `agent-spawn.test.ts` now covers the prompt-resolution seam, the isolation contract (`buildClaudeArgs`, `buildCodexArgs`, `isolateAgentEnv`/`agentEnv` and the auth families), the credential-store-aware lookups (`captureClaudeTranscript`, `findNewestCodexRollout`) and one real spawn through a fake CLI on PATH. Uncovered: `rolloutMatchesCwd` in full (`.252`–`.255`) plus `.245` spawnTee/spawnTeeAsync forwarding, `.246` combinedOutput, `.251` mid-walk ENOENT tolerance, `.256` ensureTranscriptDir idempotence, `.259`/`.260` the two leg-runner compose-and-capture semantics, `.261` the `cwdFilter` passthrough and `.350` the 0-byte capture rule. The cwd-filter four are the ones to write first: every dev-loop.test.ts scenario injects `steps.runImplementer`/`runReviewer`/`runReadiness`/`runMergeResolver` fakes that bypass `runClaudeLeg`/`runCodexLeg` entirely, so the load-bearing mechanism for "transcripts are attributed to the right issue under N-way concurrency" has no test in this area at all.
- **leg-supervisor.ts (the actual detached tree-kill process) has no standalone test file.** It is only exercised end-to-end through `leg-timeout.test.ts`, which spawns it as a real child process and observes outcomes — so its cap/idle/kill-tree behaviors ARE integration-tested, but internal branches (missing argv[2] exit 64, a spawn() throw for the leg command itself, the double-`finish()` idempotence guard, `writeFileSync` failure tolerance) are never independently forced.
- **dev-loop-supervised.ts's own pure decision function `nextSupervisorAction` is well-tested; the skills gate it consults, `skillsStageNeeded`, lives with the report's writer in `install-skills.ts` and is covered there (.201–.205), including through real runs of both modes.** `main()` is driven as a real subprocess from two directions — the `--rehearsal` close (`notification-coverage.test.ts`, .319/.320) and one relaunch of the real child, taken for the footprint it leaves on the target repo (`dev-loop-supervised.test.ts`, .365) — but always as a means to another assertion: the relaunch loop's own semantics stay unasserted, and the inline stall counter is only ever RIDDEN (it is what bounds the footprint case), never checked against .212's expectations.
- **The CLI entrypoint blocks of dev-loop.ts** (`if (import.meta.url === ...)`) — assertCleanTree and the final exit-code logic (0/1/2) — are exercised only by the pure `runLoop`/`runLoopParallel` calls inside tests; the module is invoked as a real subprocess (`node dev-loop.ts`) in exactly two places, both `dev-preflight.test.ts` cases behind row .190, which reach the loop's own baseline precondition rather than any of the documented exit codes. The supervisor's relaunch behavior therefore still has no test proving the child produces the exit codes its `res.status` logic depends on.
- **Merge-integrity interacts with the frozen-artifact guard in an untested combination**: a merge conflict that the resolver leg fixes (S10) where the CONFLICT ITSELF is on a frozen path is never separately tested — `defaultResetWorktreeFrozenArtifacts` is asserted to neutralize frozen edits BEFORE the first merge attempt and again before the retried merge, but no test forces a frozen-path conflict specifically into the merge-resolver flow (only a non-frozen-path conflict is exercised in the merge-conflict tests, and only a non-conflicting frozen edit is exercised in the frozen-artifact tests — the two are never combined).
- **Quota-aware retry and per-leg timeout are two independent watchdogs that can both apply to the same leg but are never tested together**: a leg that BOTH rate-limits (triggering `runLegWithQuota`'s wait-and-retry) AND separately times out (triggering `leg-timeout.ts`'s cap/idle kill) on a later attempt has no combined test — each mechanism is verified in isolation only.

### factory/cleanup-tree.ts

- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.326] A tree a child process keeps writing into while it is being removed: a single-shot `rmSync(recursive, force)` throws ENOTEMPTY at that instant, whereas `cleanupTree` re-invokes the WHOLE recursive removal on a bounded linear backoff and converges once the writer stops (node's own `maxRetries`/`retryDelay` cannot serve here — the racing entries spend that budget during the walk; see AGENTS.md "Platform traps") | single-shot throws ENOTEMPTY; `cleanupTree` returns true and the tree is gone | unit, race/platform-trap | cleanup-tree.test.ts ("a single-shot removal loses the race a bounded retry wins")
- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.327] A writer that outlives every attempt | `cleanupTree` returns false and NEVER throws; the tree is left standing rather than half-reported as gone | unit, error-branch | cleanup-tree.test.ts ("a writer that outlives every attempt leaves the tree standing and never throws")
- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.328] A tree a writer keeps racing is announced on fd 2 naming its path, registered, and retried at exit (up to EXIT_ATTEMPTS = 3 bounded attempts) — by then every child is reaped — and the drain stays silent about a tree something else already removed (no false "removed" line) | host process stderr carries `survived N removal attempts (ENOTEMPTY — …); up to 3 more attempts at exit` then `removed at exit: <path>`; the tree is gone; the host's exit code is untouched | integration (child process), resources/orphans | cleanup-tree.test.ts ("a tree a writer keeps racing is announced with its path and removed at exit, once the writer is reaped")
- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.329] Replay safety: a path that never existed, and a second cleanup of an already-removed tree | both report success (force), no throw, nothing registered as a leftover | unit, idempotence | cleanup-tree.test.ts ("an absent path and an already-removed tree are both successes")
- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.330] A populated tree with no writer racing it | removed on the first attempt, reports success | unit | cleanup-tree.test.ts ("removes a populated tree and reports success")
- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.332] ENOTEMPTY is AMBIGUOUS and the announcement must not assert a cause: a subdirectory whose permissions deny removal reports the very same code as a live writer (node surfaces that inner EACCES as a non-empty parent), so the reason names both candidates and nothing more; clearing the permission lets the exit drain converge | `(ENOTEMPTY — entries keep reappearing or resist removal — a live writer, or a subdirectory that denies removal)` then `removed at exit: <path>` | integration (child process), message honesty | cleanup-tree.test.ts ("an obstruction that is no writer at all … reports the same ENOTEMPTY with both causes named")
- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.333] A target whose PARENT denies removal (EACCES) | the reason is the permissions one and no live writer is ever claimed — an operator is not sent hunting a process when the fix is a chmod | integration (child process), message honesty | cleanup-tree.test.ts ("a target whose parent denies removal reports the permissions reason, never a racing writer")
- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.334] A failure no retry can clear (a non-string path -> ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE, i.e. any code absent from the retryable table) | fails fast after exactly ONE attempt, still returns false instead of throwing, announces `was not removed after 1 removal attempt (…); nothing further will retry it`, and promises NO exit retry (nothing registered, no drain line) | unit + integration (child process), boundary/invalid-input | cleanup-tree.test.ts ("a failure nothing can retry (a path that is not a string) …")

### Area cross-notes

- **Serial-suite lock contention across files, not just within one file.** `control.spec.ts`, `settings.spec.ts`, `layout-edit.spec.ts`, and `overflow.spec.ts` are EACH individually `test.describe.configure({mode:"serial"})`, and all target the SAME demo server/port for a given browser project. Playwright's `fullyParallel: true` + `workers: 4` means these four files can still run CONCURRENTLY as separate files against the same demo server, each internally serial but racing each other's writes to the same on-disk settings/run-lock/yml. Nothing in the config file-level `test.describe.configure` scope prevents inter-FILE races — only intra-file ordering is guaranteed. This is a structural GAP: no evidence anywhere (config or spec comments) that cross-file serialization on the shared demo target is actually enforced beyond "hope the timing doesn't collide," despite the file-level comments only ever reasoning about intra-file races.
- **The onboarding chooser's untested Modes A/C/D (open-existing, import-docs, talk-to-Vivi) are the single biggest coverage hole in the onboarding surface** — only Mode B (scaffold) is driven end-to-end; the other three intake/acquisition paths are asserted present but never clicked through, meaning a broken import or Vivi-chat intake flow would not be caught by e2e at all.
- **`clickPastOverlap`'s `force: true` is used pervasively as the standard idiom for mobile-Sheet/scroller overlap**, but the same escape hatch would silently mask a genuinely-disabled control if ever misapplied — this is a latent risk shared across control.spec.ts, settings.spec.ts, sidebar-legend-minimap.spec.ts, and smoke.spec.ts, not a single-file issue.
- **The screenshot-based specs (xbrowser-screenshots and the two fixed-frame captures inside settings.spec.ts) are documentation captures, not visual-regression gates** — none of the PNG outputs across this area are ever diffed against a baseline or against each other. This is a consistent, area-wide gap: "prove the whole UI works across browsers" (the xbrowser file's own stated goal) is only partially met — presence/reachability is proven by the preceding assertions, but the actual PIXEL content is never verified, only captured for human review.
- **Global-setup's fixture materialization order is a hidden dependency chain**: long-target creation depends on demo-target materialization having already succeeded in the SAME globalSetup call (guarded by `existsSync`), and nothing else depends on that order. A partial failure early in `globalSetup` degrades every later step silently rather than aborting the whole matrix loudly — this cross-cuts overflow.spec.ts (whose whole `long` shape is that copy) and is not guarded by any single test.
- **The rehearsal harness (`dev-rehearsal.ts`) and the two fixtures (`formula`, `pocket-ledger`) constitute Vivicy's OWN meta-test-suite** — they are the mechanism that proves the whole freeze -> extract -> dev-loop -> merge -> ledger chain works end-to-end, self-tested against the factory's own tooling. Because this harness is itself "the test," there is no higher-level test-of-the-tests: a subtle bug in one of the ~15 chained assertions inside `dev-rehearsal.ts` (e.g. the weak `passingGates === totalIssues` COUNT-only check noted in the ISSUE-0001…ISSUE-0013 cross-notes, or the unexercised `dependencyOrderRespected` false-branch) would not itself be caught by any other test in this area — the rehearsal harness has no meta-rehearsal. This is the deepest structural gap in the whole area: correctness of the verifier of correctness is unverified.
- **Neither fixture's `--dry --concurrency>1` path is exercised by any package.json script** — `factory:rehearsal` and `factory:rehearsal:formula` both default to sequential (concurrency=1); the parallel-worktree scheduler is only ever exercised by someone manually running `node factory/dev-rehearsal.ts --dry --concurrency=N`, which means CI (as configured via package.json alone) likely never runs the concurrent path at all for either fixture.

### Adversarial additions

- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.X1] `main()` is invoked bare at the bottom of `factory/dev-rehearsal.ts` (`main();`) with no `.catch`/`.then` attached — an unhandled rejection anywhere in the async body (e.g. the dynamic `import(pathToFileURL(...dev-loop.ts))` at stage 5 rejecting because the temp repo's `dev-loop.ts` resolution fails, or the dynamic `import("../lib/development-overlay.ts")` inside `projectLedgerOntoMap` throwing) surfaces as a raw Node unhandled-rejection stack trace and a non-standard exit path, bypassing the harness's own clean-failure reporting (`writeReport` + the `[FAIL]` stage log) entirely | GAP: no test drives a genuine throw from either dynamic `import()` call site to confirm the harness degrades to its own report-then-exit-1 path rather than an uncaught-rejection crash — this is distinct from the already-noted `.241` guard, which only covers the temp-workspace-vanished case (an explicit `existsSync` check on the ledger file), not an arbitrary async throw elsewhere in `main` | unit, error-branch, process-exit-hygiene | GAP
- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.X2] Stage 4 (`generate-viewer-data (pre-loop)`) calls `generatedData(temp)` — an un-guarded `readJson` (via `JSON.parse(readFileSync(...))`) — immediately after the `sh(...)` child-process call, with NO try/catch around it, even though the preceding `record(...)` for that same stage hasn't executed yet: if `generate-viewer-data.ts` exits 0 but writes truncated/malformed JSON (e.g. killed mid-write by an OOM or an external process, or a bug that emits a partial file), `JSON.parse` throws synchronously and crashes the ENTIRE rehearsal script before stage 4's own `record()` call is reached — a data-corruption bug in the driven script is reported as a total harness crash with no PASS/FAIL row at all, rather than a named "generate-viewer-data (pre-loop)" FAIL | GAP: no test feeds a truncated/malformed architecture-data.json through this exact call site to confirm it fails as a clean stage-FAIL rather than an uncaught JSON.parse exception aborting the whole run | unit, error-branch, malformed-input | GAP
- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.X3] `readMapFromHead` and `readJsonFromHead` (both used only in the stage 7b(a) closure assertion) collapse TWO distinct failure modes into the same `null` return: (a) `git show HEAD:<path>` exiting non-zero because the path was never committed, and (b) the git command succeeding but its stdout being unparsable JSON (a corrupted git object or an in-flight commit race) — both are swallowed by the same `catch { return null }`, so the closure record's detail string (`committedVerified` = 0 either way) cannot distinguish "map isn't tracked yet" from "map IS tracked but its committed content is unreadable," which are very different bugs to chase | GAP: no test isolates the JSON-parse-failure branch specifically (only the "not tracked at all" shape is implicitly exercised by a normal passing run) — a maintainer debugging a real closure-assertion failure gets no signal on which of the two branches fired | unit, error-branch, weak-diagnostic | GAP

- [e2e-test-infra-rehearsal.X5] The rehearsal's fixed integer sleep in the async dry legs (`delay(15)` in both `dryImplementerParallel`/`dryReviewerParallel`) is the ONLY mechanism making concurrency "real rather than merely scheduled" per the file's own comment — on a sufficiently fast/idle CI runner, Node's microtask/timer scheduling could still resolve all N dry legs before any of them observably overlaps (i.e. the 15ms delay is a heuristic, not a guaranteed interleaving), so the `.237`/`.239` concurrency assertions (settle-once, dependency-order) could pass even in a build where the scheduler regressed to fully sequential execution disguised as parallel | GAP: no test asserts an actual wall-clock overlap (e.g. two issues' start/end timestamps genuinely intersecting) — only the OUTCOME (no duplicates, correct order) is checked, never that true concurrent execution occurred | e2e-process, concurrency, weak-assertion | GAP

### Area cross-notes

- **Fix-context wiring is the seam most exercised end-to-end**: extract-issues.test.ts proves formatCheckOutput/formatVerdict/formatMapError/formatFixContext both as pure units AND wired live through the fix loop (attempt N+1's `checkOutput` literally equals the formatted text of attempt N's failure). This is strong coverage; the only remaining gap (extraction-gates.70) is the simultaneous-triple-failure concatenation, which cannot happen in the real gate ORDER (deterministic gates short-circuit map-gen, which short-circuits fidelity) but IS reachable directly via the exported `formatFixContext` pure function and is untested there.
- **The five deterministic gates (semantic, traceability, spike, reference, change-control) are exercised as REAL implementations inside extract-issues.test.ts**, not mocked — so a regression in any gate's exit-code contract (e.g. semantic-extraction-check returning exitCode 0 with placeholder:true, which extract-issues additionally treats as non-green via `!semantic.placeholder`) would be caught by the orchestrator tests even without a matching unit test in the gate's own file. This means extraction-gates.50 is well covered at the integration seam even though semantic-extraction-check.ts's OWN test file has no test asserting that exact `!semantic.placeholder` orchestrator-side behavior (it only tests the checker's own exitCode:0/placeholder:true contract in isolation, correctly).
- **spike-check.ts and spike-prover.ts share the transitive-gated_by graph logic** (`transitiveGatedBy`, topological concerns) as two SEPARATE local implementations (spike-check.ts's own `transitiveGatedBy` + spike-prover.ts's own `transitiveGatedBy`) — a DRY violation the test suite does not flag, and a future edit to one chain-walk without the other risks the two modules disagreeing on what "transitively verified/provable" means. No test cross-validates that spike-check's `transitivelyVerifiedGates` and spike-prover's chain-gate check agree on the same corpus in every case (only that each independently behaves correctly on its own fixtures).
- **extract-issues.ts's spike-verification gate reads `transitivelyVerifiedGates` from spike-check.ts directly** (not from spike-prover's own per-run live view) — so a spike proved earlier IN THE SAME runSpikeProving call is correctly seen (spike-prover updates the file, transitivelyVerifiedGates re-reads from disk), but this cross-module hand-off (spike-prover flips file -> extract-issues re-reads via a fresh transitivelyVerifiedGates(repoRoot) call after proving completes) has no dedicated integration test proving the spike-verification check sees a spike VERIFIED DURING THIS RUN's proving stage (extraction-gates.21's "PROCEEDS to green" test seeds an already-verified spike rather than one flipped verified by the (stubbed) proving stage in the same call) — soft GAP.
- **excerpt-drift.ts's impure entry point `runExcerptDrift` is completely untested** (extraction-gates.197-201) despite being the one function in the file that touches the filesystem and is presumably wired into the Change-Control re-extraction flow — all four existing tests in excerpt-drift.test.ts exercise only the pure helpers (`excerptMap`, `compareExcerpts`, `formatExcerptDrift`). Given extract-issues.ts's own reopen path (extraction-gates.86) is also a GAP, this suggests the whole "Change-Control re-extraction reopens changed-excerpt issues" life-cycle is exercised nowhere in this area's test files, only presumably in a separate change-control.test.ts / reopen.test.ts outside this area's scope.
- **The four prompt files are pure LLM instructions** with no executable test surface of their own; the only meaningful "tests" for them are consistency checks against the deterministic parsers/checkers they promise to satisfy (generate-viewer-data.ts's YAML grammar, the verdict JSON shapes read by extract-issues.ts/spike-prover.ts). None of these consistency checks exist as automated tests today — they are currently guaranteed only by the fixture corpus (rehearsal/pocket-ledger) incidentally satisfying a subset of the schema, which is a much weaker guarantee than a schema-conformance test that walks the prompt's documented shape against the parser's accepted grammar systematically (e.g. fuzzing every documented enum value, every optional/required field).
- **CLI entry points across ALL SIX executable files** (extract-issues.ts, semantic-extraction-check.ts, traceability-check.ts, reference-check.ts, spike-check.ts) are almost entirely untested except semantic-extraction-check.ts (which has 2 CLI tests). The "no VIVICY_TARGET_ROOT configured -> exit 2" branch and the "exit code mirrors result.exitCode" branch are repeated, nearly-identical dead test debt across 5 files (extraction-gates.72-75, 93, 168-169, 187-188, 232-233) — a single shared e2e-process test helper parametrized over the 5 CLI entry files would close all of these gaps with minimal duplication.

### Area cross-notes

- **Ledger validation failure is unhandled in the read path (highest-severity GAP).** `/api/map`'s `readLedger()` only guards `readFile`/`JSON.parse` failures with try/catch (route.ts:96-104), but `applyLiveOverlay` → `deriveDevelopmentOverlay` throws plain `Error`s for a wide range of semantically-invalid-but-syntactically-valid ledgers (unknown graph_ref, duplicate graph_item_state, verified-without-gate-evidence, in_progress-without-heartbeat — all in development-overlay.ts). None of these throws are caught anywhere between `applyLiveOverlay` and the route's `Response.json`, so a single malformed ledger entry — plausible after a partial write, a bug in the dev-loop writer, or manual editing — takes down the ENTIRE map viewer with an opaque 500, contradicting the module's own "read path is tolerant... never 500s" doc comments (map-data.ts:214, 244). This applies to both the mocked unit test (route.test.ts) and the real-stack integration test (route.live-overlay.test.ts) — neither exercises an invalid ledger. See cases .116, .193, .199.
- **`Promise.all` vs. the "never blocks the others" claim in map-review.ts.** The module doc comment (map-review.ts:8) and `runMapReview`'s own inline comment ("A lens whose leg dies or writes nothing simply contributes no findings (never blocks the others)") describe fault-isolation semantics, but the implementation fans out via `Promise.all`, which aborts on the FIRST rejection rather than isolating it. If a real lens-spawning leg throws (agent process crash, spawn failure), the entire map review run fails instead of degrading to 7/8 lenses. Either the implementation needs `Promise.allSettled` + per-leg catch, or the comment overpromises; either way this is untested and worth a dedicated case. See .272.
- **Two independently-maintained copies of `slugGraphRefPart`/graph-ref formulas that must never drift**, called out explicitly at `development-overlay.ts`'s `slugGraphRefPart` (implicit in generate-viewer-data.ts via `getNodeGraphRef`/`getEdgeGraphRef`). No test asserts the two produce identical output for the same input — a manual sync risk with zero automated backstop. Additionally, `normalizeMapData`'s OWN THIRD graph_ref default formula (`edge:${from}->${to}`, simpler, no relation/protocol) at map-data.ts:158-161 diverges from both — three formulas, one is a fallback used only when `edge.graph_ref` is absent from the parsed JSON (which in practice should never happen since the generator always emits it), but nothing prevents/tests the divergence if a hand-edited or third-party JSON omits it. See .110, .259.
- **`validateMap` (the ~300-line business-rule gate in generate-viewer-data.ts) has essentially zero direct test coverage** — the existing `generate-viewer-data.test.ts` file tests ONLY `parseArchitectureMap` and `reconcileLayout`, both pure syntax-level concerns. Every semantic invariant that keeps the architecture map internally consistent and honest (status must be not_started, no evidence_refs on the target map, canonical-file coverage, frozen-baseline pinning, kind/lane/status referential integrity, the anti-"fallback" banned-term check, high-risk line precision) is exercised by NO automated test in this repo area. This is the single largest coverage gap in the whole area and should be prioritized — a regression here would silently let an invalid architecture-map.yml reach production (or, conversely, block a valid one) with no test signal at all. See .229-.259.
- **`main()` — the actual CLI entrypoint — is completely untested**, including the `--reconcile-against` and `--write-map-metadata` flags, the layout-preservation assertions it wires together, and the final `writeFileSync` of the generated artifact. Every constituent pure function it calls is tested in isolation (except `validateMap`, see above) but the orchestration itself has zero coverage; a wiring bug (wrong argument order, skipped assertion call, wrong file path) would not be caught. See .223-.225.
- **Component-level (architecture-map.tsx) filter/selection/save logic is entirely untested** despite the underlying pure helpers in lib/map-data.ts and lib/map-layout-save.ts being well covered — there is no `architecture-map.test.tsx` in this area's file list at all. Every piece of UI wiring (filter combination → visible node/edge sets, click handlers, edit-mode drag/save state machine, edge-label drag math, ClusterBackdrops group computation/drag) is a GAP. This is the largest UI-side coverage gap; recommend at minimum a React Testing Library suite covering filter combinations, selection round-trips, and the save-error/dirty-tracking state machine (cases .1-.58).
- **`StatusDot` silently produces an unstyled (no background class) dot for a garbage status string** rather than falling back to `bg-border` — the `?? "not_started"` nullish-coalesce only catches `null`/`undefined`, not an arbitrary invalid string, and `BG_BY_STATUS[garbage]` is `undefined`, which `cn()` simply drops. Low blast radius (the type system should prevent this upstream) but worth one boundary test given how cheap it is to add. See .85.
- **`MapNodeData.ownsData` truncation to 3 entries has no visual "+N more" affordance** and no test confirms this is the intended (vs. accidental) UX — worth a design/product check alongside the test gap. See .66, .60.

- [map-ui-data-viewer.X8] `nodeMinimapColor` / `MiniMap` boundary: a node whose `data.color` is present but is not a valid `ColorToken` shape (e.g. a partial object missing `border`, from a version-skewed cached React Flow node during a hot-reload) — `nodeStrokeColor={(n) => nodeMinimapColor(n).border}` would pass `undefined` straight to React Flow's SVG `stroke` attribute since `nodeMinimapColor` only null-coalesces a MISSING `color` object, not a malformed one with individual missing fields | expected: never render an `undefined` stroke (SVG silently no-strokes, reintroducing the "empty minimap" bug the palette tests explicitly guard against for the KNOWN-kind case, but not for a malformed color object) | kind: unit | GAP
- [map-ui-data-viewer.X9] `ArchitectureMap`'s `onNodesChange`/`onEdgesChange` (wired straight to React Flow's default reducers via `useNodesState`/`useEdgesState`) are never asserted to LEAVE the position/selection sync effects intact when React Flow internally fires a `remove` change (e.g. user presses Delete/Backspace while a node is focused, which React Flow supports by default since `nodesFocusable` is not disabled) — nothing in the code or tests proves a node cannot be deleted from the LOCAL `nodes` state via a stray keypress while `data.nodes` (the source of truth) still lists it, potentially desyncing the two on the next `flowNodes` recompute (the `useEffect` sync only PRESERVES a dragging position, it does not defend against a node having been removed from local `nodes` entirely — the effect would just re-add it from `flowNodes` on the next data-driven re-render, but between that recompute and the deletion there could be a render where the deleted node is simply gone from the DOM with no user-visible explanation) | expected: keyboard delete either is explicitly disabled (`nodesFocusable={false}` / `deleteKeyCode={null}`) or is proven harmless by a test; today neither the disabling prop nor a regression test exists | kind: e2e-ui | GAP
- [map-ui-data-viewer.X10] `saveLayout`'s fetch call has no `AbortController`/timeout and no guard against a user toggling `editMode` off (or navigating away / the target project changing via a background poll) WHILE a save is in flight — the `saving` -> `saved`/`error` state transition still fires against the (possibly stale/unmounted) component's closures (`setSaveStatus`, `setSaveError` reference the render's own setters, which in React are stable, but `nodesById`/`edgesById`/`nodePositions` are captured in the closure at call time, not re-read) — a target-project SWITCH mid-save (a real workflow: user drags a node, clicks Save, then immediately switches the open project via the top-left picker before the fetch resolves) would complete a layout write against the file paths resolved server-side for whatever `getTargetRoot()` returns AT THE TIME THE REQUEST ARRIVES, which could now be the NEW target — i.e. a save initiated against project A can land on project B if the switch completes before the in-flight POST is received | expected: either the request carries an explicit target identifier that the server validates against, or the client aborts in-flight saves on project switch; neither exists today, and there is no test simulating a target switch during a pending save | kind: integration | GAP
