### Area cross-notes

- **Governance has no half-acquired window at all.** The folder is the server's spawn-time binding, so nothing is chosen, remembered or reported up: `POST /api/project/govern` either governs that one folder or refuses, and success is a full page reload into the workspace branch of the same route. There is no callback to fire twice and no target to forget. `govern-gate.test.tsx` covers the success/refusal wiring and `e2e/onboarding.spec.ts` drives the whole gate → workspace → Vivi chain.
- **FolderBrowser is reused by four contexts with different `disabled`/`allowCreate` wiring** (the in-panel governed open-existing: no `allowCreate`, `disabled=selecting`; the Start-governance target picker and the map-empty import target-pick: `allowCreate` + `requireGoverned={false}`) — no test asserts that only the govern/import target-picks show the New-folder affordance while the governed-open browser omits it, which is the entire reason the contexts share one component instead of forking it.
- **Scaffold no longer selects anything**: `scaffoldProject` ends by DESCRIBING the folder it just wrote (`describeProject`), never by persisting a selection — the coupling that used to make a scaffold a global state change is gone, and the only remaining TOCTOU is the describe racing a folder deleted between the last write and the return, which yields a typed `ProjectError` rather than a half-selected project.
- **fs-browser.ts and project.ts both implement "must be absolute, existing, real directory" validation independently** (`resolveBrowsePath` vs `describeProject`) with different error-code enums (`FsBrowseError` vs `ProjectError`) — not literally duplicated logic (different concerns: browse-anywhere vs is-a-project-root) but no cross-test proves the two never diverge in what "a directory" means (e.g. one resolving symlinks and the other not: `describeProject` does NOT realpath/resolve symlinks the way `resolveBrowsePath` does — a symlinked project root would describe/persist the SYMLINK path, not the canonical one, which is inconsistent with the browser's canonicalization guarantee). This is a real, non-obvious asymmetry — flagged as a GAP.
- **The scaffold API route trusts the lib entirely for validation ordering** (name validated before target dir, per `scaffoldProject` source order) — the route-level test only proves the codes map correctly, not the actual precedence, which lives untested at the route/integration boundary (only implicitly at the lib level, and not even explicitly there either — see GAP list).
- **No End-to-end (e2e-ui / Playwright) tests were found for this entire onboarding surface** in the read files (only component-level Testing-Library tests exist for the forms themselves). Given the task mentions `e2e/*.spec.ts` exists in the repo, this area's actual E2E coverage should be checked outside this file list — everything marked `e2e-ui` above is a GAP relative to the files in scope, but may be covered by files outside this area (e.g. `e2e/onboarding.spec.ts`) not included in the read set.

- [onboarding-project-scaffold.374] `ensureManagedBlock` (Buffer in, Buffer out — see .410) is TOTAL — it never throws on any input, so damaged markers self-repair instead of dead-ending governance (deleting a block whole already self-heals; punishing a half-deletion was incoherent). Vivicy owns a span only when its begin and end are each other's NEAREST counterpart — an end pairs with the closest begin above it, never across an intervening begin — plus any marker LINE left unpaired; everything else is the owner's. ### Area cross-notes (additional)

- **The base matrix significantly under-verified its own e2e-ui GAP claims.** Every row labeled `e2e-ui | GAP` was asserted without checking whether `e2e/*.spec.ts` files actually exist for this area, despite the task's own file list implying they should be checked. `e2e/onboarding.spec.ts` exists and does cover the four-cards-visible assertion and the full Mode-B (scaffold) happy-path flow end to end — those two rows are corrected above from GAP to COVERED. All other e2e-ui rows remain genuine gaps (no e2e coverage found for Mode A/import/Vivi-chat paths, folder-browser interactions, or any dialog's error/validation states).
- **No test anywhere in this area exercises TWO concurrent requests to the same mutating endpoint** (`POST /api/project/govern`, `POST /api/fs/mkdir`) — both mutations are check-then-act without locking. The launcher's own mutations are the exception and the precedent: every `/api/projects` action rides the registry's stage lock, which is what makes two tabs opening one project deterministic.
- **`describeProject`'s symlink asymmetry (finding #302/#301 above) is the single most concrete, easily-reproducible gap in the whole area** — unlike most "theoretical" TOCTOU/race gaps, this one is deterministic and trivial to write a test for (symlink a temp dir, call `describeProject` on the link, assert `root` against `realpathSync`), and it directly touches the registry key contract every launcher action depends on.
- **Every `detectGateCommand`/scaffold precedence rule (package.json before Makefile, empty-string test script counting as detected) is fully unverified** — the function has real decision branches (`return` early on package.json even if it's a hollow signal) that no test distinguishes from "detected a real thing."

## Area: upload-vivi-chat

Scope: `lib/import-docs.ts`, `lib/import-docs.test.ts`, `app/api/project/govern/route.ts`, `lib/vivi.ts`, `lib/vivi.test.ts`, `app/api/vivi/route.ts`, `app/api/vivi/sessions/route.ts`, `app/api/vivi/sessions/[sessionId]/route.ts`, `app/api/vivi/card/route.ts`, `factory/vivi-turn.ts`, `factory/prompts/vivi.md`, `components/chat/vivi-panel.tsx`, `components/chat/vivi-panel-context.tsx`, `components/chat/decision-card.tsx`, `components/chat/menu-card.tsx`, `components/chat/menu-card.test.tsx`, `components/chat/vivi-panel.test.tsx`, `components/chat/decision-card.test.tsx`, `components/chat/message-bubble.tsx`, `components/chat/markdown.tsx`, `components/chat/message-bubble.test.tsx`. The acquisition half is a dumb-fast `startGovernance`: `POST /api/project/govern` receives a multipart target with OPTIONAL documents, refuses an already-governed target, lays the governance scaffold (reusing `lib/scaffold.ts`), and — when docs are present — explodes zips, filters by the server type allowlist, writes `.vivicy/uploads/<batch-id>/` + a per-batch `manifest.json` (hashes + dominant language, detected deterministically by extracting binary-doc text via the shared `lib/text-extract.ts` before `franc`), and emits an append-only notification; with zero docs it governs-only (no batch). There is NO agent leg at import time; a residual-`und` batch is resolved later by a fast Codex leg at the head of doc-prep (`factory/detect-language.ts`), which atomically updates the manifest language. The launcher bubble + left overlay panel host Vivi chat; the onboarding view is inventoried in the onboarding area, the notifications feed in the workflow-notifications area.

## Cross: cross-journeys

Scope: greenfield AND brownfield (non-empty repo) journeys through Vivicy's real UI, grounded in the actual modules (`lib/control.ts`, `lib/vivi.ts`, `lib/import-docs.ts`, `factory/dev-loop.ts`, `factory/dev-loop-supervised.ts`, `factory/install-skills.ts`, `factory/cr-apply.ts`, the sidebar/project/chat/crs/notifications/workflow components, and `e2e/**`). Every case cites the files whose behavior it exercises.

Format: `[id] | scenario | expected outcome | kind | covered-today`

## Cross: cross-chaos-process

Grounded in: `lib/control.ts`, `lib/project-runtime.ts`, `lib/spawner.ts`, `lib/vivi.ts`, `lib/import-docs.ts`, `factory/dev-loop-supervised.ts`, `factory/dev-loop.ts`, `factory/progress-ledger.ts`, `factory/atomic-write.ts`, `factory/target-root.ts`, `factory/install-skills.ts`, `factory/cr-apply.ts`, `app/api/control/{start,stop,resume,retry-stage}/route.ts`, `e2e/control.spec.ts`.

Key mechanism inventory that every scenario below cites:
- **run-state.json** (per-project `<target>/.vivicy/runtime/run-state.json`; `lib/control.ts` `claimRunLock`/`isRunActive`/`readRunState`): O_EXCL `wx` claim, liveness = `spawner.isAlive(pid)` (real: `process.kill(pid,0)`), stale lock auto-cleared on next claim attempt only (no background sweep).
- **skills-install.lock** (per-project `<target>/.vivicy/runtime/skills-install.lock`; `lib/stage-lock.ts` `claimStageLock`, claimed by the STAGE in `factory/install-skills.ts` and only PROBED — `stageLockHolder` — by `lib/control.ts` and `factory/cli.ts`): same O_EXCL + pid-liveness pattern, independent of run-state.json.
- **skills-report.json phase liveness** (`lib/control.ts` `isSkillsInstallInFlight`, `SKILLS_STALE_MS=15min`): a second liveness signal for the SAME stage, based on `updated_at` staleness rather than pid — the lock and the report can disagree.
- **.integration.lock** (`factory/dev-loop.ts` `withIntegrationLock`/`acquireExclusiveLock`/`reclaimStaleExclusiveLock`, `INTEGRATION_LOCK_STALE_MS=120s`): in-process async mutex + O_EXCL file lock, reclaimed on staleness OR dead pid; 30s acquire timeout.
- **progress-ledger.json.lock** (`factory/progress-ledger.ts` `acquireLock`/`reclaimStaleLock`, `LOCK_STALE_MS=30s`, `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_MS=10s`) + revision CAS (`CAS_MAX_ATTEMPTS=50`).
- **atomicWriteJson** (`factory/atomic-write.ts`): temp-file + rename; only atomic within one filesystem.
- Worktrees under `.vivicy-worktrees/<issue-id>` (`factory/dev-loop.ts` `defaultCreateWorktree`): idempotent create (force-removes stale worktree/branch first).
- The Next server and the factory process are **fully decoupled**: `startSupervisor`/`startSkillsInstall` use `spawner.spawnDetached`, so killing the Next (UI) process never touches the detached child; only `stopSupervisor` (an explicit API call) sends SIGTERM to the recorded pid.

Kept as a measured residual rather than closed by publishing the lock through a temp and a link: that would trade the single exclusive create every client's refusal is pinned on for a new temp-residue class, on a window narrower than any probe can observe. | unit | GAP |

### E. VIVI CHAT — Next kill mid-turn

### I. Stale-lock matrix (dead vs. alive pid, by lock type)

- [cross.chaos-process.28] | `run-state.json` names a DEAD pid (process crashed without SIGTERM cleanup) — the common "kill -9'd the wrong process" or OOM-killed supervisor case. | `isRunActive` (`lib/control.ts:348-354`) calls `spawner.isAlive(deadPid)` -> false -> `clearRunState()` -> returns false. A subsequent `startSupervisor` call's `claimRunLock` sees the EEXIST on its first `wx` write, calls `isRunActive` (false, and ALREADY clears the file as a side effect), then retries the `wx` write which now succeeds cleanly (no race window against itself since it's sequential in one call) — a completely clean recovery path, unit-tested already. | unit | `lib/control.test.ts` "allows a restart once the prior pid is no longer alive (stale lock)" (line 136). |
- [cross.chaos-process.29] | `run-state.json` names an ALIVE pid but belonging to an UNRELATED process (pid got reused by the OS after the real supervisor died, e.g. long-uptime machine, pid wraparound). | `isAlive`/`process.kill(pid,0)` has no way to distinguish "this pid IS my supervisor" from "this pid happens to be alive as some other program" — `isRunActive` would report `true` (falsely "running") and refuse a genuine restart with `already_running`, requiring a human to manually delete `run-state.json` (or wait for that unrelated pid to also exit) since there is no secondary identity check (e.g. a process-start-time or a command-line match) anywhere in `lib/control.ts`. | e2e-process | GAP — PID-reuse false-positive is an inherent design limitation, not just an untested path; worth flagging explicitly. |
- [cross.chaos-process.30] | `.integration.lock` is DEAD-pid-stale (parallel-loop child crashed while holding it) vs. ALIVE-but-past-`INTEGRATION_LOCK_STALE_MS` (a genuinely slow merge/gate exceeding 120s). | `reclaimStaleExclusiveLock` (`factory/dev-loop.ts:2311-2330`) reclaims on EITHER condition (`tooOld || dead`) — so a slow-but-alive holder (e.g. a merge-resolver leg legitimately taking >120s under heavy load) gets its lock FORCE-STOLEN by a waiting sibling even though it is still working, a genuine correctness risk: two processes could then believe they both hold the integration critical section (the original holder never checked its OWN lock is still valid before proceeding — it just runs to `finally { unlinkSync(lockPath) }` unconditionally, `factory/dev-loop.ts:2280-2288`, meaning the ORIGINAL holder's `unlinkSync` at the end would delete the SECOND holder's freshly-reclaimed lock file, and the original holder's in-process work (already past the stale check) continues believing it's still safe). | unit | GAP — critical: a slow-but-alive integration-lock holder can be double-entered past the 120s staleness window; the in-process mutex (`integrationMutexes`) only serializes within ONE Node process, so this is real for a KILLED-AND-RESPAWNED loop process racing the ORIGINAL loop process if somehow both are alive (e.g. supervisor relaunches the child while the old child is a lingering zombie that hasn't actually exited) — flag as critical. |
- [cross.chaos-process.31] | `skills-install.lock` DEAD pid vs. `skills-report.json` phase still "installing" (report not yet stale by its own 15-min clock). | The pid probe reads a dead holder as free regardless of the report's own staleness clock, and the next STAGE reclaims the file — the pid check is authoritative and STRICTER (immediately on death, not after 15 minutes), so this direction (lock says dead, report says "recent") is SAFE; the dangerous direction is the reverse (scenario 13: lock says alive, report looks stale) which is NOT symmetric. | unit | GAP (the stage's reclaim half is covered at [cli-supervisor-process-infra.372]; the report-vs-lock disagreement is not) |
- [cross.chaos-process.32] | Progress-ledger lock (`progress-ledger.json.lock`) held by a DEAD pid vs. an ALIVE-but-slow writer (CAS retry storm under N=12 parallel, all racing to write near-simultaneously). | `reclaimStaleLock` (`factory/progress-ledger.ts:279-309`) uses the SAME `tooOld || ownerDead` OR-reclaim pattern as the integration lock (scenario 30) with a SHORTER stale window (30s vs 120s) — under N=12 parallel with heavy CAS contention (`CAS_MAX_ATTEMPTS=50`, `LOCK_RETRY_MS=25`ms retries), a genuinely busy-but-alive writer holding the lock for its write+CAS-retry-loop could in principle approach 30s if the ledger has grown large and 50 CAS attempts each re-read+re-write it, risking the same "stale reclaim on a still-alive slow holder" hazard as scenario 30, just with a tighter margin. | unit | GAP — same class of hazard as .30, flag together. |

### Critical GAPs (ranked by blast radius)

1. **No lock at all guards `runExtract`/extraction** (`lib/control.ts:518-552`, scenarios 2 and 35). Every other long-running/stateful factory stage (`startSupervisor`, `startSkillsInstall`) has an O_EXCL pid-liveness lock; extraction has none, so two browser tabs, a UI+CLI pair, or a killed-and-retried request can spawn overlapping `extract-issues.ts` runs against the same target with no serialization, racing canonical/baseline/issue-corpus writes. This is the highest-blast-radius gap in the whole cross-cutting surface.


2. **`.integration.lock` and the progress-ledger lock can force-steal from a still-alive-but-slow holder** (`factory/dev-loop.ts:2311-2330`, `factory/progress-ledger.ts:279-309`, scenarios 30/32). Both reclaim on `tooOld OR dead`, not `tooOld AND dead`; a legitimately slow (not crashed) merge/gate/CAS-retry-storm under high parallelism (N up to 12) can have its lock stolen by a waiting sibling while still working, risking two holders believing they own the critical section simultaneously — the exact failure mode the lock exists to prevent.

3. **`runViviTurn` has zero mutual exclusion around its snapshot/spawn/diff window** (`lib/vivi.ts`, scenario 17). Unlike the ledger (O_EXCL+CAS) or the integration merge (dedicated lock), two concurrent Vivi turns — even on different sessions, since enforcement scope is the whole `.vivicy` tree — can have their snapshot-before / diff-after windows interleave, causing one turn's legitimate write to be misattributed to (or misrejected as a violation by) the other turn's diff.

4. **Deleting a project's runtime dir mid-run silently defeats that project's locks** (scenario 40). `run-state.json`, `skills-install.lock` and the notify log all live under that project's `.vivicy/runtime/`; removing it makes every liveness check report "nothing running" even while the supervisor, the parallel dev-loop and a skills install are all genuinely alive headless. The blast radius is now one project, never all of them at once.

## Maintenance (automatic updates)

**The rule: every code change that adds, changes, or removes behavior MUST update this matrix in the same working session.** No exceptions, no "later". Concretely:

- New behavior → add its cases (scenario | expected | kind | GAP or the test you wrote) under the right area, at the next free id.
- Changed behavior → update the affected cases' scenario/expected text; if the covering test changed, update the covered-today reference.
- Removed behavior → delete the case lines (ids are retired, never reused).
- New test written for an existing case → flip its `GAP` to the `covered-today: <file> ("<test name>")` reference.
- Update the **status table** counts for every touched area in the same edit.

This obligation is wired into `AGENTS.md`, so every agent session working on Vivicy is bound by it — and it is machine-enforced: `scripts/test-matrix.test.ts` fails `npm test` when behavior sources change without a reconciliation re-stamp (`npm run matrix:stamp`, which records the content fingerprint + the HEAD commit), listing via git exactly which files changed since the stamped commit. The matrix stays current because an unreconciled behavior change turns the suite red.

### Priority GAPs to burn down next (ranked by blast radius)

1. **No lock guards extraction at all** — [cross.chaos-process.2], [cross.chaos-process.35], [cross.chaos-process.1]. Two tabs, UI+CLI, or a killed-and-retried request can spawn overlapping `extract-issues.ts` runs against the same target with zero serialization, racing canonical/baseline/issue-corpus writes. Every other stateful stage (`startSupervisor`, `startSkillsInstall`) has an O_EXCL pid-liveness lock; `runExtract` has none. Product fix + tests.
2. **Stale-lock reclaim can steal from a slow-but-alive holder** — [cross.chaos-process.30], [cross.chaos-process.32], [cross.chaos-parallel-merge.37], [cross.chaos-parallel-merge.30]. Both `.integration.lock` (120s) and the progress-ledger lock (30s) reclaim on `tooOld OR dead`, so a legitimately slow merge/gate/CAS-storm under N=12 can be double-entered — the exact failure the locks exist to prevent. Verify intent, then test (or fix to require dead-pid AND staleness).
3. **`runViviTurn` has zero mutual exclusion around its snapshot/spawn/diff window** — [cross.chaos-process.17], [cross.journeys.25]. Two concurrent Vivi turns (even different sessions — enforcement scope is the whole `.vivicy` tree) can misattribute each other's writes, corrupting allowlist enforcement/rollback. Also: no end-to-end test of a real allowlist violation and byte-for-byte rollback.
4. **Deleting a project's runtime dir mid-run silently defeats that project's locks** — [cross.chaos-process.40]. `run-state.json`, `skills-install.lock` and the notify log all live under that project's `.vivicy/runtime/`; wiping it makes every liveness check report idle while that project's supervisor, dev-loop and skills install keep running headless.
5. **CRITICAL error-code collision renders the wrong message to the user** — [upload-vivi-chat.248]. Four semantically distinct failures in `lib/vivi.ts` all throw `ControlError` code `"missing_target"`, so the UI shows the wrong diagnosis for three of them. Product fix + tests.
6. **No diff-scope enforcement on the CR-applier leg** — [baselines-change-requests.223], [baselines-change-requests.196]. Unlike Vivi's snapshot/diff/rollback, nothing detects a CR-applier leg editing outside `.vivicy/canonical/**` — an asymmetric trust model with a fully undetected out-of-bounds-edit path.
7. **Ledger validation failure is unhandled in the `/api/map` read path** — map-ui-data-viewer cross-note (highest-severity GAP of that area). `readLedger` guards read/parse only; `applyLiveOverlay` → `deriveDevelopmentOverlay` can throw on a structurally invalid ledger, turning one bad file into a total map outage (500) instead of a degraded overlay.
8. **No e2e drives the import journey end-to-end** — [cross.journeys.4], [cross.journeys.10], [cross.journeys.13]–[cross.journeys.17], [cross.journeys.88]–[cross.journeys.89]. `import-docs-flow.test.tsx` now covers the component contract (gating, single accept-list picker, per-file rejected preview, governed-refusal toast, success + language toast, `onImported`), but no Playwright spec drives docs→folder→submit from the panel or the map empty-state dialog (real multipart upload + a fresh target folder). The largest remaining e2e GAP on this surface.
